docs.title: embco
docs.text: A payables agent for the ERPNext you already run. It reads purchase orders, receipts and invoices, decides what to pay now, what to pay later, what to hold and what to ask the owner, with a written reason, and pays in USDC on Arc through Circle. The AI agent pays and reads the result; a smart contract sets how far it can go.

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text:
embco checks each invoice before it pays:

  • it compares the invoice with the order and the receipt,
  • it pays only a wallet that the supplier signed and the owner approved,
  • a contract the agent cannot change limits each payment and each week,
  • every decision goes into a journal: if someone changes an old entry, it shows.

  • How it works

    One cycle from ERPNext to the chain, and the fixed rule that decides PAY, HOLD or ASK.

  • Architecture

    The layers, the trust boundaries, and where each piece of code lives.

  • Smart contracts

    The shop contract, who can call what, and every check before a payment.

  • Connect your ERPNext

    A step-by-step guide: four small changes in ERPNext, then two keys in the dashboard.

  • Run your own server

    The same dashboard and agents on your server: one .env and one install script.

docs.title: Built on
docs.text:
• Arc and USDC. Suppliers are paid in USDC, straight from the shop owner's wallet.
  • Circle developer-controlled wallets send the agent's transactions with idempotency keys. A new shop's agent is a smart contract account whose network fees Circle Gas Station pays, so the owner never sends it gas.
  • An AI model decides which payments to make and when, sends them, reads what happened and tells the owner what only they can fix. Its payments pass through the same gate and the same contract as everything else. Today it is Claude, by Anthropic (how to use another model).
  • ERPNext stays the system of record. embco adds a Payment Entry for every payment it makes.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: The code is in the repository. The contracts and their verification are described on the contracts page.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: embco is four layers with one rule between them: the model may shape a decision, but it never releases money. The money moves only when the shop contract accepts the call.

docs.title: Trust boundaries
docs.text: Actor Can do Cannot do Owner (MetaMask wallet) Create the shop contract, set limits, approve supplier wallets, pause or resume, change the agent's address No limit applies to the owner, and every change the owner makes is public on chain Agent (Circle wallet of the shop: a smart contract account whose gas Circle pays; shops made before that have one EOA) Pay an approved supplier, within the per-payment and weekly cap, once per invoice; pause; as the owner's delegate on a chain, bring USDC from the owner's Unified Balance to the owner's own wallet on Arc Raise a limit, approve a payee, pay an unapproved wallet, pay twice, resume after a pause, send the owner's Unified Balance anywhere but the owner's wallet on Arc Supplier Sign a challenge with its wallet to prove the address is theirs Change a payee on its own: the owner still approves it AI model Decide what to pay and when, send the payment itself and act on what happened, and talk to the owner Override HOLD, pay what the checks do not allow, or bypass the contract

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
1. Money is Decimal, never float, and every amount is an exact integer on chain (6 decimals).
  2. The core talks only to LedgerAdapter, never to a specific ERP.
  3. The model starts a payment, but never alone: the checks must allow it and the contract must accept it.
  4. The limits live in a contract the agent cannot change.

The agent lives in agent/: its brain (agent.py), tools/, reflexes/, guardrails/ and memory/. What it stands on lives in services/ (ERP, Circle, payments, the hosted service). The contracts live in contracts/.

docs.title: Module map
docs.text: Package Responsibility agent/agent.py, prompt.py, think.py, plan.py The brain. When a reflex wakes it, the model (today Claude Haiku 5.5, at high effort for its rounds and medium when it answers the owner) reads a short briefing and calls tools until every open invoice has its decision: pay now, pay on a date, hold, or ask the owner, each with a reason, plus alarms and notes for later and a summary for the owner. It pays during the session and reads what happened (paid with its transaction, refused by the contract, or Circle's own error), then acts on it: looks up why, holds, or tells the owner what only they can fix. Capped per session (turns, tokens, 10 payments) and per day (USD 1 of model use by default, estimated from the tokens and the public prices; past it the agent is not woken until the next day, and the owner is told once). A payment it sent stands even if the session is cut off; its other choices count once the session finishes. The rules still decide what may be paid; the agent decides what is paid and when, and pays it. On by default, and nothing is paid without it; EMBCO_AUTONOMY=observe decides and explains without paying services/telegram The agent on Telegram, a process of its own (embco telegram). A chat is linked with a one-time code from the dashboard (hashed, 10 minutes, once); any other chat can do nothing. /stop turns the whole agent off and pauses the contract from the agent's wallet, /pause pauses payments while the agent keeps watching and answering, /status tells its state: none of them go through the model, and only the dashboard turns it on again. Any other text is a message to the agent, whose answers come back to the chat. The agent's questions about invoices arrive once: with two buttons (yes, pay it / no, hold it) when only the owner's yes is missing, where a press from the linked chat, while the question is still open, is only a message to the agent; as a reminder to use the dashboard, followed by the agent's question, when the owner's wallet is needed (approve a wallet, raise a limit, add money, authorize or resume payments). What the agent writes to the owner is one topic, short and without full hashes: a longer text goes back to the model to be rewritten. The bot token never reaches a log or an error agent/tools What the agent can call. To read: the open invoices (with the last state of each payment), a search over them (supplier, due date, what the checks say), one invoice in full, a supplier's profile, an item's price history, the cash position (with the owner's USDC on other chains), the state of a payment, and its own wallet (balance for network fees, whether the contract has it as its agent, whether the contract is paused). To act: pay now (sent at once, with the result back to the agent), deposit the owner's USDC on another chain into their Unified Balance through their ShopFunding there, estimate and bring funds from the Unified Balance to their wallet on Arc (which chains and how much are the agent's choice), schedule (on that day the agent is woken to pay), hold, ask the owner, set an alarm, keep a note, finish. To talk: reply to the owner's message, notify the owner of something to act on (at most 3 per session), and email a supplier from the shop's ERPNext, only after the owner agreed agent/guardrails/gate.py Refuses a payment the rules do not allow (HOLD, ASK, already paid, over this week's room in the contract) before anything is sent, and the refusal goes back to the agent agent/reflexes/wake.py When to wake the agent: an invoice new, changed or without its decision, a payment failed or blocked (not again for a result it already saw), the day it planned to pay something, a due date close with nothing planned, an owner answer or supplier signature, a limit change, an alarm it set, the daily round. What the agent did itself is not a reason: an invoice it paid does not wake it when it changes, an alarm about it does not ring, its own payments are not a change of money, and a hold it chose that only lost reasons since still holds. No reason, no model call services/erp Domain models, LedgerAdapter protocol, erpnext/ adapter (client, mappers, adapter). Reads, plus one write through PaymentWriter: a payment final on chain becomes a submitted Payment Entry (on testnet, a draft marked TESTNET, so test USDC never closes a real invoice), drafted by ERPNext from the invoice and checked against what was paid (party, amount, invoice) before it is written, with the transaction hash and payee wallet in its custom fields. The same transaction is never written twice agent/guardrails/controls Context builder and one small module per control: three-way match, payee wallet, duplicates, price anomaly, payment limit, supplier status. Each returns PASS, HOLD (an unproven wallet, a duplicate bill), ASK (a first payment to a new wallet) or NOTE (evidence for the agent to weigh: receipt and quantities, price, limit, disabled supplier). A wallet never paid before is held until the supplier signs a challenge with it (proof the address is right and theirs), then the owner is asked to approve, since only a person knows whether the supplier really asked for the change. The question says who set the wallet in the ERP and when, from the supplier's change history services/hub, services/shops The hosted service behind the dashboard, a process of its own (embco hub). A shop's owner signs in with their wallet; the hub creates the shop's two Circle wallets before its contract, so the contract is created with its agent: a smart contract account that is the agent and sends every transaction, with its gas paid by Circle Gas Station, and an EOA in the same wallet set that only signs the owner's Unified Balance spends as their delegate (a smart contract account cannot). A shop made before this has one EOA that does both and pays its own gas. It stores each shop's ERPNext connection encrypted, tests it, and starts, stops and restarts the shop's agent through systemd services/signing EIP-712 wallet ownership message bound to embco and Arc testnet, and signer recovery (ordinary wallets; smart contract wallets need EIP-1271 on chain) agent/guardrails/rules Fixed combining rule (HOLD, then ASK, then PAY; a NOTE changes nothing and goes to the agent as something to weigh), policy config, the weekly-budget planner and owner answers: an approved ASK becomes PAY, a rejected one HOLD, only while the decision is unchanged. The owner answers with the CLI, on the invoice in ERPNext (an owner-only field, accepted only from EMBCO_OWNER_USERS per the ERP's change history, once per question), or, for a new wallet, by approving it in the contract. HOLD is never overridden agent/memory Memory between runs, stored as changes: every run, each new or changed decision, the policy when it changes, invoices that leave the unpaid list, owner answers, wallet challenges and the signatures that answer them, AI explanations, and each payment (blocked, submitted, complete, failed, or recorded in the ERP). One append-only, hash-chained sequence; it grows with events, not with runs. DecisionJournal protocol, SQLite store agent/reflexes One cycle (verify memory, decide, apply owner answers, remember, issue wallet challenges, explain, follow payments already sent and write the final ones in the ERP, then the agent's session), the interval loop that survives an ERP outage and stops on a tampered memory, and the text report services/settings, services/cli Settings from the environment or .env, checked once, secrets never shown; the embco command: run, watch, answer, challenge, sign-wallet, history, verify, create-wallet, shop, hub, telegram agent/explain A plain-language summary and next step for each HOLD or ASK decision, through the model with structured output (today Claude Haiku 5.5, at low effort; with Claude Opus and Sonnet 5.x it also gets the server-side refusal fallback). Explained once per decision and stored; a failure is logged and retried next cycle; never changes a decision. Off unless EMBCO_EXPLAIN=on services/circle Circle developer-controlled wallets over REST: a fresh entity secret ciphertext (RSA-OAEP, SHA-256) on every write, idempotency keys, wallet creation (EOA or smart contract account), contract execution and transaction state. Reads are retried when the connection drops; errors never carry credentials services/payments Pays one invoice when the agent calls pay now, and gives back what happened, refusals and Circle errors word for word: re-reads the invoice and supplier from the ERP (same amount, USD, valid wallet), skips what the contract already marks paid or what does not fit under its weekly cap, lists for the dashboard any wallet the owner has not approved in the contract yet, including invoices asked about only because their wallet is new (approving the wallet there then counts as the owner's answer, saved in the journal like any other; a wallet approved before the question answers nothing) (EMBCO_APPROVALS_FILE: wallet, invoice and amount only, no supplier names), simulates the exact Memo.memo -> ShopPayables.pay call through the Arc node and names the contract's error if it would fail, sends the same bytes through Circle with an idempotency key per invoice and attempt, follows it to a final state, records every step, then writes it into the ERP. At most 3 failed transactions per invoice. Amounts become exact 6-decimal integers or are refused services/unified_balance The owner's Unified Balance (Circle Gateway) through Circle's Unified Balance Kit 1.8.0 and its Circle Wallets adapter, in a small Node script (kit/, pnpm, Node 22) the agent runs once per call, with Circle's credentials only in its environment. At start it gives the agent's Circle wallet the same address on each source chain (deriveWalletByAddress); then it reads the owner's balance per chain and whether the agent is a delegate there, estimates fees, and spends with the split the model chose, always minted to the contract owner's wallet on Arc through Circle's Forwarding Service. The dashboard gets the same per-chain view after each check dashboard/ Static owner page (ethers 6.17.0 vendored, no build). Connects MetaMask, adds Arc Testnet, creates the shop from the factory, and lets the owner set the allowance and limits, approve suppliers (with one click for the wallets the agent is waiting to pay, from the agent's file), choose the chains the agent can pay from (each one turned on creates the owner's funding contract there with the shop's limits, approves it and authorizes the agent in Gateway, in one batched confirmation when the wallet supports EIP-5792; Circle's Unified Balance Kit 1.8.0 with its viem adapter, bundled once into vendor/), pause or resume the agent, and read suppliers and payments from the contract's events. Money is parsed and shown as exact 6-decimal integers. Chain reads go through the site's own /rpc proxy, which adds the node credential on the server, so the page never holds one. The shop console has three columns: invoices, a short chat with the agent in the middle (a message is at most 300 characters; the details are in the activity) and the activity beside it, where the agent's reasoning is open (money that moved shows once, in the chat, as a receipt). Served with a strict Content Security Policy contracts/ (Solidity) ShopFunding, one per owner on each source chain (Base Sepolia, Ethereum Sepolia), created from ShopFundingFactory: the agent may only move the owner's USDC there into the owner's own Gateway balance, within a per-move and a weekly cap. ShopPayables, one per shop, created by its owner from ShopPayablesFactory. The money stays in the owner's wallet; the agent can only pay approved suppliers, once per invoice, within a per-payment and a weekly cap; owner or agent can pause, only the owner resumes or changes limits. Unit and fuzz tests, plus a fork test against Arc Testnet's real USDC

docs.title: ERP independence
docs.text: The core never imports ERPNext. Adding Odoo or SolidInvoice means a new adapter under services/erp/ that satisfies the same protocol.

docs.title: Model independence
docs.text: The agent talks to the AI model through two interfaces: Brain (agent/agent.py) for its decisions and Explainer (agent/explain/base.py) for the explanations. Today the only implementation is Claude, by Anthropic, which needs an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Another provider means a new class that satisfies the same interfaces. The rules, the gate and the shop contract do not change: they never depend on which model is behind them.

docs.title: Connect your ERPNext
docs.text:
This guide is for the person who runs the shop's ERPNext. You will make four small changes in ERPNext and then paste two keys into the embco dashboard. Nothing is installed on your ERPNext, and the agent never gets admin rights.

Before you start

  • Your shop is already created in the dashboard: your wallet is connected and your shop contract exists (create it in Settings). Creating it asks for one free signature and one transaction, and the shop comes with its own agent: you never set it up or send it gas.
  • You can sign in to ERPNext as an administrator (System Manager) to make the changes below.
  • Your ERPNext opens with an https:// address. embco is tested with ERPNext v16, including Frappe Cloud.

docs.title: Step 1: Create a user for the agent
docs.text:
The agent signs in to ERPNext as its own user, with only the roles it needs.

  1. In ERPNext, create a new User for the agent (for example agent@your-shop.com).
  2. Give it these three roles, and no others:
    • Accounts User
    • Purchase User
    • Stock User
  3. Open that user and, under API Access, generate its keys. ERPNext shows an API Key and an API Secret. Copy both now: the secret is shown only once.

With these roles the agent can read suppliers, purchase orders, receipts and invoices. The only thing it writes is the Payment Entry for an invoice it paid.

docs.title: Step 2: Require an order and a receipt for every invoice
docs.text:
This is what lets the agent check that what you were billed is what you ordered and received.

  1. Open Buying Settings.
  2. Set the option that requires a Purchase Order to Yes.
  3. Set the option that requires a Purchase Receipt to Yes.
  4. Save.

Both are No in a new ERPNext.

docs.title: Step 3: Make room for wallet addresses
docs.text:
A wallet address is 42 characters long, and ERPNext's bank account number field holds 30. You change this once:

  1. Open Customize Form and choose Bank Account.
  2. Find the field Bank Account No and set its Length to 64.
  3. Save.

docs.title: Step 4: Add your suppliers' wallets
docs.text:
Each supplier's wallet is saved as a bank account at a bank called USDC on Arc. The supplier's real bank account stays as it is.

  1. Create a Bank named USDC on Arc (once).
  2. For each supplier you will pay with embco, create a Bank Account:
    • Bank: USDC on Arc
    • Party Type: Supplier
    • Party: the supplier
    • Bank Account No: the supplier's wallet address (starts with 0x)

One wallet per supplier

If a supplier has two active accounts at USDC on Arc with different wallets, the agent holds its invoices and does not choose between them.

A new or changed wallet is never paid right away. The supplier first confirms it is theirs, and then you approve it in the dashboard (see What happens next).

docs.title: Step 5: Connect in the dashboard
docs.text:
1. Open app.embco.xyz and Sign in with your wallet, if you did not when you created the shop. It is a signature, not a transaction: it costs nothing.

  2. In Your ERPNext, fill in:

    Field What to write ERPNext address The address you open ERPNext with, for example https://your-shop.frappe.cloud Company Your company's name exactly as it is written in ERPNext API key The key from Step 1 API secret The secret from Step 1 Bank that holds supplier wallets USDC on Arc (already filled in) Extra payment fields Leave it empty, unless your ERPNext asks for extra fields when you submit a payment by hand (some local tax setups do). Then ask whoever set up your ERPNext which fields and values to write

  3. Click Test and connect. The dashboard tries the keys without changing anything in ERPNext, and shows each check:

    Check What it means Keys ERPNext accepted the agent's key (required) Invoices The agent can read your unpaid purchase invoices (required) Company The company name was found Payments ERPNext can draft a payment for an invoice (nothing is saved) Wallets How many supplier wallets were found at USDC on Arc

  4. A shop created before its agent came with it shows Make it the agent: click it once. This lets your shop's agent wallet pay approved suppliers, within the limits you set.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text:
• The agent checks ERPNext on its own every 15 minutes. You do not need to open anything.
  • A new supplier wallet is confirmed by the supplier at app.embco.xyz/supplier, with a signature from that wallet. Then it appears in the dashboard under Waiting for your approval. Before approving, check in ERPNext that the wallet belongs to the supplier you expect.
  • When the agent pays, it records a Payment Entry in ERPNext for that invoice. The transaction hash is in Reference No, and the wallet paid is in the remarks.
  • Other chains the agent can pay from (optional): in Settings > Which chains can the agent pay from?, click Choose chains, turn on the chains where you keep USDC (Base Sepolia, Ethereum Sepolia) and click Save. Your wallet asks once for each chain that changed when it batches calls (MetaMask with its smart account, EIP-5792), otherwise once per step, and it needs that chain's gas token (test ETH). Turning a chain on creates your funding contract there with your shop's limits, approves it, and authorizes the agent in your Unified Balance (Circle Gateway). Your USDC stays in your wallet there. When an invoice needs more than your wallet on Arc holds, the agent moves it into your Unified Balance and brings it to your wallet on Arc, choosing which chains it comes from. It never sends it anywhere else, and your limits still apply. The agent needs no gas: its network fees are paid by Circle Gas Station. After you change your shop's limits, a chain shows "save to use your shop's limits": click Save. Turning a chain off removes the approval and the agent's authorization there. What is already in your Unified Balance stays yours.
  • Telegram (optional): in the dashboard, Connect Telegram gives a code to send to the embco bot. Then /status says how the agent is, /pause pauses payments while the agent keeps watching, and /stop turns the agent off and pauses the shop contract. Only the dashboard turns it back on. Any other message goes to your agent.

docs.title: Draft mode
docs.text:
While embco runs on testnet, payments are made in test USDC. So that test USDC never closes a real invoice, each Payment Entry stays as a draft whose remarks start with "TESTNET". This is draft mode, and it is on for every new shop.

  • The dashboard shows the mode next to the agent's status: Draft mode or Submitting to ERPNext.
  • To change it, open Settings > ERPNext. Turning draft mode off asks you to confirm a second time: from then on each payment is submitted and closes its invoice, even when it was paid in test USDC, and your books show those invoices as paid.
  • Turning it back on takes one click. Each change is written in Your agent, and if the agent is on, it restarts with the new mode.

docs.title: If something does not work
docs.text: Problem What to do Keys check fails Check the address starts with https://, and generate the keys again (Step 1) Invoices check fails Check the agent's user has the three roles from Step 1 Payments check fails Try to submit a payment to a supplier by hand in ERPNext. If you cannot either, an app or a required field is blocking it (seen with a Mexican e-invoicing app). Fix that in ERPNext first, or use Extra payment fields Wallets check finds 0 Check the Bank is named exactly USDC on Arc and each Bank Account has Party Type Supplier

docs.title: Smart contracts
docs.text: The shop's limits live on chain, in a contract the agent cannot change. These are the contracts in contracts/ (Solidity 0.8.37, Arc Foundry).

docs.title: Deployed on Arc Testnet
docs.text: Contract Address ShopPayablesFactory 0x5D455dF984C85abe160E4585E0c1139ded5d2c3b (source verified on Sourcify) USDC (ERC-20 interface) 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 Memo (predeployed) 0x5294E9927c3306DcBaDb03fe70b92e01cCede505 Pilot shop's agent wallet (Circle EOA, from before shops got their own gasless agent) 0x2309ed4a43e3b1ab4222f6938538a6c88bd27dd8

docs.title: Who can do what
docs.text: The owner can also call pay, and the limits do not apply to the owner. Every other caller is refused with NotAuthorized.

docs.title: How a payment is accepted
docs.text: Each invoiceRef is a unique reference for the invoice (the contract documents a hash of its ERP name as one example), so it can be paid once and matched to its invoice. The transfer uses transferFrom: the money stays in the owner's wallet until the call succeeds, and revoking the USDC allowance stops every payment.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• maxPerPayment is greater than zero and no more than weeklyCap.
  • The weekly window starts when the shop is created and runs in seven-day blocks.
  • Only the owner changes limits. Every change emits LimitsChanged.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Event Emitted when Paid An invoice is paid, with its reference, payee, amount and caller LimitsChanged The owner changes the per-payment or weekly limit AgentChanged The owner sets the agent's address PayeeSet The owner approves or removes a supplier wallet Paused / Unpaused The agent or owner pauses; only the owner resumes

The dashboard reads these events from the chain to show suppliers and payments.

docs.title: ShopFunding: the owner's USDC on other chains
docs.text:
Chain ShopFundingFactory Base Sepolia 0x69e31Af302Ee222204AA78099D39a2956F5C95d6 Ethereum Sepolia 0x69e31Af302Ee222204AA78099D39a2956F5C95d6

ShopFunding is the same idea on a source chain of the owner's Unified Balance (Circle Gateway). Each owner creates one from ShopFundingFactory on that chain and approves it, the way they approve the shop contract on Arc.

Who Can do Cannot do Agent fund(amount): take that much of the owner's USDC and deposit it into the owner's own Gateway balance, within a per-move and a weekly cap; pause Send it anywhere else, change a limit, resume after a pause Owner Everything the agent can, with no limit; set the limits and the agent; resume Transfer ownership

The money never stays in the contract: fund takes it from the owner's wallet and calls Gateway's depositFor(usdc, owner, amount) in the same transaction, so the deposit always belongs to the owner. From there the agent, which the owner authorizes as a delegate in Gateway, brings it to the owner's wallet on Arc. Unit and fuzz tests, plus a fork test against Base Sepolia's real GatewayWallet and USDC.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: embco runs one cycle every 15 minutes (or once, on demand). Each cycle reads the shop's purchase documents from ERPNext, checks every open invoice and remembers the result. When there is something to decide, the AI model is woken: it decides, pays what it chose to pay (if payments are on), sees what happened and acts on it.

docs.title: The fixed rule
docs.text:
Each control returns a finding. Only two kinds stop an invoice, and no model can change them: HOLD (the supplier's wallet is missing, invalid or not confirmed by the supplier's signature, or the bill repeats one already entered) and ASK (a first payment to a new wallet, answered by the owner). Everything else a control finds (a missing receipt, less received than billed, a price jump, an amount over the per-payment limit, a disabled supplier) is a NOTE: evidence the AI agent weighs before it decides to pay, hold or ask the owner.

Checks are small: one control per file under agent/guardrails/controls/. Each one returns a finding with its evidence, so the reason on screen is the reason the rule used.

docs.title: Who decides what
docs.text:
Question Decided by Notes Can the invoice be paid at all? The rules Only a wallet not yet proven or approved, or a duplicate bill, stops it. Fixed, testable, no model involved Does what was billed make sense? The AI model It weighs the notes (receipt, quantities, price history, limits) and pays, holds or asks the owner, with its reason Is this supplier's wallet safe? The wallet control, then the owner A new wallet waits for the supplier's signature and the owner's approval What is paid now, and what waits for a date? The AI model It pays itself and reads the result; the gate refuses anything the rules forbid before it is sent The owner's wallet on Arc is short: bring money from which chains? The AI model It reads the owner's Unified Balance on other chains and the fees of each split, and brings what it chooses. It only ever lands in the owner's own wallet on Arc, from chains where the owner authorized it A payment did not go out: why, and who fixes it? The AI model It looks up the reason with its tools and tells the owner what only they can fix Is the payment allowed on chain? The shop contract Limits, approved payee, once per invoice, pause

Nothing leaves the owner's wallet until the owner authorizes payments in the dashboard and makes the shop's agent wallet the agent of the contract.

docs.title: When the wallet on Arc is short
docs.text:
The owner may keep USDC on other chains too (Base Sepolia, Ethereum Sepolia). In the dashboard, under Which chains can the agent pay from?, the owner turns on the chains they want to use.

When an invoice needs more than the owner's wallet on Arc holds, the agent:

  1. looks at the owner's USDC on each chain, and at the fee of each way to move it,
  2. chooses where to take it from and how much,
  3. moves it into the owner's Unified Balance (Circle Gateway) and brings it to the owner's wallet on Arc,
  4. pays the invoice.

The money only goes to the owner's own wallet, and only from chains the owner turned on. On each of those chains a contract of the owner sets how much the agent can move at once and per week. The agent pays no gas: Circle covers its network fees.

docs.title: Memory
docs.text: Every decision, owner answer, wallet challenge and payment step is an event in an append-only journal. Each event stores the hash of the one before it, so changing an old event breaks the chain. embco verify checks it.

docs.title: Owner answers
docs.text:
When the agent asks, the owner answers in one of three places. Each answer counts once and only for the question the agent last showed:

  • the dashboard: approving a new wallet in the shop contract is also the answer,
  • the ERP, on the invoice, from an account listed in EMBCO_OWNER_USERS,
  • the command line, with embco answer.

On Telegram the owner can talk to the agent, pause payments or stop it, but an answer to a question still goes through one of the three places above.

See Connect your ERPNext for the ERP side.

docs.title: Run your own server
docs.text:
This guide sets up what runs behind app.embco.xyz on a server of your own: the dashboard, the hub (the API the dashboard uses to connect shops) and one agent per shop. Shop owners then use your dashboard exactly as they use app.embco.xyz: they create their shop contract, connect their ERPNext and set their limits there.

What you need

  • A server with Ubuntu or Debian (tested on Ubuntu 24.04), and a user with sudo.
  • A domain pointing to the server, with ports 80 and 443 open. The dashboard gets its HTTPS certificate on its own.
  • A Circle account with developer-controlled wallets: an API key and a registered entity secret.
  • An Anthropic API key, for the AI model that decides.
  • An Arc Testnet node URL.
  • Optional: a Telegram bot token from @BotFather.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/JaDi03/embco.git
cd embco
cp .env.example .env
nano .env
sudo bash deploy/install.sh

In .env, write your domain in EMBCO_SITE and fill in the node URL and the keys. Each line has a short note.

The script checks .env before it installs anything, and says what is missing. It ends with Done. Open https://your-domain: open it, and the dashboard asks to connect a wallet. From there, shop owners follow Connect your ERPNext.

Save the shop key

The script creates /etc/embco/shops.key, which encrypts each shop's connection on disk. Save a copy now, apart from any other backup, as below.

docs.title: Update or change a setting
docs.text:
The same command, from the same folder, updates everything and keeps your settings:

cd embco
sudo bash deploy/install.sh

The script moves .env to /etc/embco/embco.env, so no copy with your keys stays in the folder you cloned. To change a setting, edit that file, or write a new .env in the folder, and run the command again.

docs.title: Back up and move to a new server
docs.text:
Moving the shops to a new server takes two things, kept in different places so that neither one alone is of any use:

  1. The shop key. It never changes, so you save it once, in a password manager:

    sudo cat /etc/embco/shops.key

  2. The shops' data (settings, connection and journal), backed up as often as you like, with the agents stopped for a moment so the journals are complete:

    sudo systemctl stop 'embco-shop@*'
sudo tar czf embco-shops.tar.gz /var/lib/embco/shops
sudo systemctl restart embco-hub

    Restarting the hub starts the agents again. Keep the file off the server.

On the new server, put both back before you install, then install as usual:

sudo install -d -m 700 /etc/embco
sudo nano /etc/embco/shops.key            # paste the key from your password manager
sudo tar xzf embco-shops.tar.gz -C /
git clone https://github.com/JaDi03/embco.git
cd embco
cp .env.example .env
nano .env
sudo bash deploy/install.sh

The script keeps the restored key, gives the files to the embco user, and the hub starts the agents of the shops whose owners left them on. Point your domain to the new server first.

docs.title: What the script sets up
docs.text:
What Where The code, run by its own system user embco, which can only write its own data /opt/embco The server's settings and the shop key, readable only by root and embco /etc/embco Each shop's settings, ERPNext keys (encrypted) and journal /var/lib/embco/shops The hub, the Telegram bot and one agent per shop, restarted if they stop systemd: embco-hub, embco-telegram, embco-shop@<contract address> A rule that lets the hub start, stop and restart the shops' agents, and nothing else polkit The dashboard with HTTPS, /api to the hub and /rpc to your Arc node, whose URL stays on the server Caddy

The hub starts a shop's agent when its owner connects ERPNext in the dashboard. If Caddy already serves other sites on the server, the script adds the dashboard next to them.
